Today's default prompt runs kmctl's audit skill, which checks only the
`.okf/` concepts that are due, and never `docs/`. Replace it with three
audits, each a prompt file the agent runs separately:

- `new:action/prompts/docs-vs-code.md`: every page in `docs/` against the
  code it describes (commands and flags against the CLI's real `--help`,
  how-tos against `action.yml` and the workflows, paths and defaults
  against the files).
- `new:action/prompts/okf-vs-code.md`: every concept in `.okf/` (not
  handoffs) against the code its claims name; all concepts, not only those
  due. `run`'s default prompt.
- `new:action/prompts/okf-vs-docs.md`: `.okf/` against `docs/`, for places
  where the two disagree (a decision says one thing, a how-to another).

A tutorial, `new:docs/tutorials/audit-your-repository-with-the-agent.md`,
written with the write-docs skill, takes a reader from nothing to a read
report: run `action/agent.py run` locally with `--prompt-file` for one of
the three audits and a provider key, open `report.md`, read one finding
(the claim, the lines that contradict it, the fix) and the checked list,
look up a citation, then write a prompt of their own with `--context`,
and last turn it on in CI. Its sample output comes from a real run. The
fields of `report.json` and what each severity means are listed in it, and
section 5 of `docs/how-to/install-the-plugin-and-the-ci-action.md` links to
it and stops saying the default audits only the concepts that are due.

`.github/workflows/knowledge-audit.yml` runs the audit and publish jobs as
a matrix over the three, each with its own artifact and issue title.
`action.yml`, `docs/how-to/install-the-plugin-and-the-ci-action.md` and ADR
0017 (a correction) follow.

Done when a live run of each prompt on a copy of the repo with planted
false claims (at least three per audit) reports each planted claim,

# audit-prompts

Relayed from: none

## Intent

Today's default prompt runs kmctl's audit skill, which checks only the
`.okf/` concepts that are due, and never `docs/`. Replace it with three
audits, each a prompt file the agent runs separately:

- `new:action/prompts/docs-vs-code.md`: every page in `docs/` against the
  code it describes (commands and flags against the CLI's real `--help`,
  how-tos against `action.yml` and the workflows, paths and defaults
  against the files).
- `new:action/prompts/okf-vs-code.md`: every concept in `.okf/` (not
  handoffs) against the code its claims name; all concepts, not only those
  due. `run`'s default prompt.
- `new:action/prompts/okf-vs-docs.md`: `.okf/` against `docs/`, for places
  where the two disagree (a decision says one thing, a how-to another).

A tutorial, `new:docs/tutorials/audit-your-repository-with-the-agent.md`,
written with the write-docs skill, takes a reader from nothing to a read
report: run `action/agent.py run` locally with `--prompt-file` for one of
the three audits and a provider key, open `report.md`, read one finding
(the claim, the lines that contradict it, the fix) and the checked list,
look up a citation, then write a prompt of their own with `--context`,
and last turn it on in CI. Its sample output comes from a real run. The
fields of `report.json` and what each severity means are listed in it, and
section 5 of `docs/how-to/install-the-plugin-and-the-ci-action.md` links to

`.github/workflows/knowledge-audit.yml` runs the audit and publish jobs as
a matrix over the three, each with its own artifact and issue title.
`action.yml`, `docs/how-to/install-the-plugin-and-the-ci-action.md` and ADR

Done when a live run of each prompt on a copy of the repo with planted
false claims (at least three per audit) reports each planted claim,
recorded in a spike.

## Could invalidate this plan

- A Flash-class model may miss planted drift in one run over a whole
  folder; then the plan needs runs per page or a stronger default model.
  Settled by spike:audit-prompts/1 and spike:audit-prompts/2: the drafts
  caught 8 of 9 plants (docs-vs-code 3/3, okf-vs-docs 3/3, okf-vs-code
  2/3, missing a default in a Correction); with okf-vs-code saying every
  option, default and number, Correction sections included, is a claim of
  its own, it caught 3/3 in 135 of 200 requests. The 8 findings that were
  not plants are real drift on main; no false positives.
- The evidence check (real-audits) accepts only lines read or found by
  search, not shell output, so docs-vs-code cannot cite the CLI's `--help`
  directly; its findings must cite the source line that defines a flag.
  If that makes the docs audit miss real drift, the check needs a way to
  cite command output. Settled by spike:audit-prompts/1: a flag renamed in
  `docs/reference/commands.md` was caught, cited against the source in
  `src/kmctl/__init__.py`.
